leads.title: God's first speech from the whirlwind - the wild animals ↔ The chargers
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The warhorse with thundering mane paws the valley, laughs at fear and says 'Aha!' at the trumpet (weight 6.7). Pair score 6.7.

Only in God's first speech from the whirlwind - the wild animals: Catalogue of wild animals (mountain goat, wild ass, wild ox, ostrich, horse, hawk, eagle) beyond human control; The eagle nests on the crag; where the slain are, there it is, and its young drink blood; The ostrich leaves her eggs in the dust, forgetting a foot may crush them, for God deprived her of wisdom; The wild ass, set free by God, laughs at the city's tumult and hears no driver's shout; The wild ox (re'em) will not serve man, plow the furrow or spend the night at his crib; By God's wisdom the hawk soars and spreads its wings toward the south; Only God knows when the mountain goats and hinds give birth and counts their months; The birds above them spreading and folding their wings: none holds them up but the Merciful; God provides prey for the lion and food for the raven's young that cry to him.

Only in The chargers: Oath by charging war-horses that pant, strike sparks with their hooves, raid at dawn, raise dust and storm into the midst of a host; Man will be evidence against himself, even if he offers his excuses; The hoofbeats of galloping horses depicted in poetry; At the end the graves are overturned and their contents scattered out (bu'thirat); God knows the secrets of the heart (ta'alumot lev); Woe to every slanderer and backbiter (humaza lumaza) who amasses and counts wealth, thinking it makes him immortal; A series of oaths by natural phenomena (dawn, night, day, sun, moon, sky, earth, stars, winds) opens or punctuates a passage.
